newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Troubled Vietnam bank wins state support -paper.
newsitem.headline: Troubled Vietnam bank wins state support -paper.

text.p: Vietnam's cash-strapped Viet Hoa bank has resumed normal operations after winning support from the state, and plans to bolster its capital by selling shares to foreign banks, the Finance and Market daily said on Wednesday.
"...with the state bank's support Viet Hoa bank has returned to normal operations and the situation has been stabilised," it said without giving details of the central bank's intervention.
Industry sources say that the sudden death of the Ho Chi Minh City-based bank's chairman, Tran Tan Tai, just over two months ago had triggered a run on deposits at Viet Hoa.
The bank has declined to comment on its financial health.

A central bank official confirmed Viet Hoa's shareholders agreed at an extraordinary meeting last Sunday to increase the bank's registered capital to 100 billion dong ($8.58 million) from 70 billion, and add new members to the management board.
The official said shares worth 33 billion dong had been earmarked for sale to foreign banks, and that two banks had already expressed an interest in buying shares.

Foreign bankers believe that Viet Hoa, which is majority owned by ethnic Chinese in Ho Chi Minh City's Cholon district, is just one of several privately held banks that have had a cash crunch in recent months.
